reference_sql:
SELECT p.product_id, ph.list_price_eur
FROM products p
JOIN price_history ph ON ph.product_id = p.product_id AND ph.valid_to IS NULL
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM competitor_prices cp WHERE cp.product_id = p.product_id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM competitor_prices cp
    WHERE cp.product_id = p.product_id
      AND cp.price_eur <= ph.list_price_eur
  )
alternatives:
SELECT p.product_id, ph.list_price_eur
FROM products p
JOIN price_history ph ON ph.product_id = p.product_id AND ph.valid_to IS NULL
WHERE ph.list_price_eur < (
  SELECT MIN(cp.price_eur)
  FROM competitor_prices cp
  WHERE cp.product_id = p.product_id
)

WITH lowest_check AS (
  -- one row per checked product
  SELECT product_id, MIN(price_eur) AS min_price_eur
  FROM competitor_prices
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT ph.product_id, ph.list_price_eur
FROM price_history ph
JOIN lowest_check l ON l.product_id = ph.product_id
WHERE ph.valid_to IS NULL
  AND ph.list_price_eur < l.min_price_eur

other_way.sql:
SELECT p.product_id, ph.list_price_eur
FROM products p
JOIN price_history ph ON ph.product_id = p.product_id AND ph.valid_to IS NULL
WHERE ph.list_price_eur < (
  SELECT MIN(cp.price_eur)
  FROM competitor_prices cp
  WHERE cp.product_id = p.product_id
)
other_way.tradeoff: Comparing with the lowest check in one subquery is shorter, but hides that a product with no checks drops out.
